# The map tells a story.

Explore certified results from the June 2026 gubernatorial primary, primary turnout, and the 2024 presidential vote. Hover over a county for the details behind each shade.
:::

::: {.maps-hero-note}
<span class="maps-hero-number">58</span>
<p>California counties<br><strong>Three interactive views</strong></p>
<span class="maps-data-tag">OFFICIAL RETURNS</span>
:::
:::

```{r}
#| label: map-data
#| include: false

library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(leaflet)
library(plotly)
library(readxl)
library(sf)

counties <- sf::st_read("data/ca-counties-2024.gpkg", quiet = TRUE) |>
  sf::st_transform(4326)

check_counties <- function(data, label) {
  missing <- setdiff(counties$NAME, data$county)
  extra <- setdiff(data$county, counties$NAME)
  if (length(missing) > 0 || length(extra) > 0 || nrow(data) != 58) {
    stop(
      label, " does not match all 58 California counties. Missing: ",
      paste(missing, collapse = ", "), "; unexpected: ",
      paste(extra, collapse = ", ")
    )
  }
}

number_value <- function(x) {
  suppressWarnings(as.numeric(gsub(",", "", as.character(x))))
}

governor_book <- as.data.frame(read_excel(
  "data/ca-2026-primary-governor.xlsx",
  sheet = 1,
  col_names = FALSE,
  .name_repair = "minimal"
))
governor_rows <- seq(3L, by = 3L, length.out = 58L)
governor_counties <- trimws(as.character(governor_book[[1]][governor_rows]))
candidate_names <- trimws(gsub("[\r\n]+", " ", as.character(governor_book[1, -1])))
candidate_parties <- trimws(as.character(governor_book[2, -1]))

governor_candidates <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(governor_rows), \(i) {
  votes <- vapply(governor_book[governor_rows[i], -1], number_value, numeric(1))
  data.frame(
    county = governor_counties[i],
    candidate = candidate_names,
    party = candidate_parties,
    votes = votes,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}))
governor_results <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(governor_candidates, governor_candidates$county), \(x) {
  x <- x[order(-x$votes), ]
  if (nrow(x) < 2L || x$votes[1] == x$votes[2]) {
    stop("The 2026 governor results contain a tied or incomplete county contest: ", x$county[1])
  }
  total <- sum(x$votes)
  data.frame(
    county = x$county[1],
    winner = x$candidate[1],
    winner_party = x$party[1],
    winner_votes = x$votes[1],
    winner_share = 100 * x$votes[1] / total,
    runner_up = x$candidate[2],
    runner_up_votes = x$votes[2],
    runner_up_share = 100 * x$votes[2] / total,
    total_votes = total,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}))
check_counties(governor_results, "The 2026 governor results")

participation_text <- pdftools::pdf_text(
  "data/ca-2026-primary-voter-participation.pdf"
) |>
  paste(collapse = "\n")
participation_lines <- unlist(strsplit(participation_text, "\n"))
participation_rows <- participation_lines[grepl(
  "^\\s*[A-Za-z][A-Za-z ]*\\*{0,2}\\s{2,}[0-9,]+\\s",
  participation_lines,
  perl = TRUE
)]
participation_rows <- participation_rows[!grepl("^\\s*State Total", participation_rows)]
turnout_counties <- gsub(
  "\\*+", "",
  sub("^\\s*(.*?)\\s{2,}.*$", "\\1", participation_rows, perl = TRUE)
)
turnout_fields <- lapply(participation_rows, \(line) {
  strsplit(sub("^\\s*.*?\\s{2,}", "", line, perl = TRUE), "\\s+")[[1]]
})
turnout <- data.frame(
  county = turnout_counties,
  registered_voters = vapply(turnout_fields, \(x) number_value(x[3]), numeric(1)),
  ballots_cast = vapply(turnout_fields, \(x) number_value(x[6]), numeric(1))
) |>
  mutate(turnout_pct = 100 * ballots_cast / registered_voters)
check_counties(turnout, "The 2026 voter participation table")

president_book <- as.data.frame(read_excel(
  "data/ca-2024-general-president.xlsx",
  sheet = 1,
  col_names = FALSE,
  .name_repair = "minimal"
))
president_rows <- seq(3L, by = 3L, length.out = 58L)
president_counties <- trimws(as.character(president_book[[1]][president_rows]))
president_candidates <- trimws(gsub("[\r\n]+", " ", as.character(president_book[1, -1])))
president_parties <- trimws(as.character(president_book[2, -1]))
democratic_column <- which(president_parties == "DEM")
republican_column <- which(president_parties == "REP")
if (length(democratic_column) != 1L || length(republican_column) != 1L) {
  stop("The 2024 presidential workbook does not identify a unique Democratic and Republican candidate.")
}
voting_patterns <- data.frame(
  county = president_counties,
  democratic_candidate = president_candidates[democratic_column],
  republican_candidate = president_candidates[republican_column],
  democratic_votes = vapply(president_rows, \(r) number_value(president_book[[democratic_column + 1L]][r]), numeric(1)),
  republican_votes = vapply(president_rows, \(r) number_value(president_book[[republican_column + 1L]][r]), numeric(1))
) |>
  mutate(
    two_party_votes = democratic_votes + republican_votes,
    democratic_share = 100 * democratic_votes / two_party_votes,
    republican_share = 100 * republican_votes / two_party_votes,
    dem_margin_pp = democratic_share - republican_share
  )
check_counties(voting_patterns, "The 2024 presidential results")

governor_map <- counties |>
  left_join(governor_results, by = c("NAME" = "county")) |>
  mutate(
    leader_group = case_when(
      winner_party == "DEM" ~ "Democratic",
      winner_party == "REP" ~ "Republican",
      TRUE ~ "Other party"
    )
  )
turnout_map <- counties |>
  left_join(turnout, by = c("NAME" = "county"))
patterns_map <- counties |>
  left_join(voting_patterns, by = c("NAME" = "county"))

party_colors <- c(
  "Democratic" = "#2d6d99",
  "Republican" = "#b24c51",
  "Other party" = "#bd9144"
)
leader_groups <- names(party_colors)[names(party_colors) %in% governor_map$leader_group]
turnout_palette <- colorNumeric(
  palette = c("#eff6fb", "#a9cce5", "#24618e"),
  domain = c(0, 100)
)
margin_palette <- colorNumeric(
  palette = c("#b5414d", "#f7f3e8", "#286f9e"),
  domain = c(-100, 100)
)
map_bounds <- sf::st_bbox(counties)

make_map_base <- function(data) {
  leaflet(data, options = leafletOptions(
    preferCanvas = TRUE,
    scrollWheelZoom = FALSE,
    minZoom = 4,
    maxZoom = 10
  )) |>
    addProviderTiles("CartoDB.PositronNoLabels") |>
    fitBounds(map_bounds["xmin"], map_bounds["ymin"], map_bounds["xmax"], map_bounds["ymax"])
}

format_votes <- function(x) {
  format(x, big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE, trim = TRUE)
}

governor_map$hover_html <- paste0(
  "<strong>", htmltools::htmlEscape(governor_map$NAME), " County</strong><br>",
  "<b>County leader:</b> ", htmltools::htmlEscape(governor_map$winner),
  " (", htmltools::htmlEscape(governor_map$winner_party), ")<br>",
  "<b>Votes:</b> ", format_votes(governor_map$winner_votes),
  " (", sprintf("%.1f%%", governor_map$winner_share), ")<br>",
  "<b>Runner-up:</b> ", htmltools::htmlEscape(governor_map$runner_up),
  " — ", format_votes(governor_map$runner_up_votes),
  " (", sprintf("%.1f%%", governor_map$runner_up_share), ")<br>",
  "<b>All candidates:</b> ", format_votes(governor_map$total_votes)
)
turnout_map$hover_html <- paste0(
  "<strong>", htmltools::htmlEscape(turnout_map$NAME), " County</strong><br>",
  "<b>Turnout:</b> ", sprintf("%.1f%%", turnout_map$turnout_pct), "<br>",
  "<b>Ballots cast:</b> ", format_votes(turnout_map$ballots_cast), "<br>",
  "<b>Registered voters:</b> ", format_votes(turnout_map$registered_voters)
)
patterns_map$hover_html <- paste0(
  "<strong>", htmltools::htmlEscape(patterns_map$NAME), " County</strong><br>",
  "<b>", htmltools::htmlEscape(patterns_map$democratic_candidate), ":</b> ",
  format_votes(patterns_map$democratic_votes), " (",
  sprintf("%.1f%%", patterns_map$democratic_share), " of two-party vote)<br>",
  "<b>", htmltools::htmlEscape(patterns_map$republican_candidate), ":</b> ",
  format_votes(patterns_map$republican_votes), " (",
  sprintf("%.1f%%", patterns_map$republican_share), " of two-party vote)<br>",
  "<b>Democratic margin:</b> ", sprintf("%+.1f pp", patterns_map$dem_margin_pp)
)
```

## 2026 governor primary

::: {.map-card}
::: {.map-card-heading}
<p class="map-kicker">01 · CERTIFIED RESULTS</p>

### Which candidate led in each county?

County colors show the party of the leading candidate in California's June 2, 2026 gubernatorial primary. Hover to see the county leader, runner-up, votes, and each candidate's share of all votes cast in the county contest.
:::

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| out-width: 100%

make_map_base(governor_map) |>
  addPolygons(
    fillColor = ~unname(party_colors[leader_group]),
    fillOpacity = 0.88,
    color = "#fffdf8",
    weight = 1,
    opacity = 1,
    label = lapply(governor_map$hover_html, htmltools::HTML),
    labelOptions = labelOptions(direction = "auto", textsize = "13px"),
    highlightOptions = highlightOptions(
      weight = 2,
      color = "#142b45",
      bringToFront = TRUE,
      fillOpacity = 1
    )
  ) |>
  addLegend(
    position = "bottomright",
    colors = unname(party_colors[leader_groups]),
    labels = leader_groups,
    title = "County leader's party",
    opacity = 0.95
  )
```

<p class="map-explainer"><strong>How to read it.</strong> California's top-two primary includes candidates from all parties. This map identifies the highest-vote candidate within each county; it does not show the statewide top two or imply a general-election winner.</p>

<p class="map-source"><strong>Sources:</strong> California Secretary of State, <a href="https://www.sos.ca.gov/elections/prior-elections/statewide-election-results/primary-election-june-2-2026/statement-vote">June 2, 2026 Statement of Vote</a>, Governor by County (XLSX); county boundaries: U.S. Census Bureau, <a href="https://www.census.gov/geographies/mapping-files/time-series/geo/tiger-line-file.2024.html">2024 TIGER/Line County shapefile</a>.</p>
:::

## 2026 primary turnout

::: {.map-card}
::: {.map-card-heading}
<p class="map-kicker">02 · VOTER PARTICIPATION</p>

### Where did registered voters turn out?

Blue shading shows June 2026 primary turnout for each county. Hover for the percentage and its official ballot and registration counts.
:::

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| out-width: 100%

make_map_base(turnout_map) |>
  addPolygons(
    fillColor = ~turnout_palette(turnout_pct),
    fillOpacity = 0.88,
    color = "#fffdf8",
    weight = 1,
    opacity = 1,
    label = lapply(turnout_map$hover_html, htmltools::HTML),
    labelOptions = labelOptions(direction = "auto", textsize = "13px"),
    highlightOptions = highlightOptions(
      weight = 2,
      color = "#142b45",
      bringToFront = TRUE,
      fillOpacity = 1
    )
  ) |>
  addLegend(
    position = "bottomright",
    pal = turnout_palette,
    values = ~turnout_pct,
    title = "Ballots cast /<br>registered voters",
    labFormat = labelFormat(suffix = "%"),
    opacity = 0.95
  )
```

<p class="map-explainer"><strong>How it is calculated.</strong> Turnout is ballots cast divided by registered voters, using the Secretary of State's county participation table. Its registered-voter denominator is based on the 15-day registration report; the state's footnote notes that same-day registration can occur through Election Day.</p>

<p class="map-source"><strong>Source:</strong> California Secretary of State, <a href="https://www.sos.ca.gov/elections/prior-elections/statewide-election-results/primary-election-june-2-2026/statement-vote">June 2, 2026 Statement of Vote</a>, Voter Participation Statistics by County. County boundaries: U.S. Census Bureau, <a href="https://www.census.gov/geographies/mapping-files/time-series/geo/tiger-line-file.2024.html">2024 TIGER/Line County shapefile</a>.</p>
:::

## 2024 presidential vote

::: {.map-card}
::: {.map-card-heading}
<p class="map-kicker">03 · HISTORICAL GENERAL ELECTION</p>

### Where was the presidential vote competitive?

The red-to-blue scale shows the two-party margin between Kamala Harris and Donald Trump in the November 5, 2024 general election. Near-neutral counties were more competitive; zoom or hover for both candidates' votes and shares.
:::

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| out-width: 100%

make_map_base(patterns_map) |>
  addPolygons(
    fillColor = ~margin_palette(dem_margin_pp),
    fillOpacity = 0.88,
    color = "#fffdf8",
    weight = 1,
    opacity = 1,
    label = lapply(patterns_map$hover_html, htmltools::HTML),
    labelOptions = labelOptions(direction = "auto", textsize = "13px"),
    highlightOptions = highlightOptions(
      weight = 2,
      color = "#142b45",
      bringToFront = TRUE,
      fillOpacity = 1
    )
  ) |>
  addLegend(
    position = "bottomright",
    pal = margin_palette,
    values = ~dem_margin_pp,
    title = "Democratic − Republican<br>two-party margin",
    labFormat = labelFormat(suffix = " pp"),
    opacity = 0.95
  )
```

<p class="map-explainer"><strong>How to read it.</strong> Margin is the Democratic candidate's share minus the Republican candidate's share, calculated among votes for those two candidates only. A positive margin favors Harris; a negative margin favors Trump. Other candidates are excluded from this two-party comparison.</p>

### The closest county margins

These are the ten counties where the 2024 Democratic–Republican two-party margin was nearest to zero.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| out-width: 100%

closest_counties <- voting_patterns |>
  arrange(abs(dem_margin_pp)) |>
  slice_head(n = 10) |>
  arrange(dem_margin_pp)
closest_counties$county_axis <- factor(
  closest_counties$county,
  levels = closest_counties$county
)

margin_chart <- ggplot(
  closest_counties,
  aes(
    x = dem_margin_pp,
    y = county_axis,
    color = dem_margin_pp
  )
) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "#9c927e", linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_point(size = 3.5) +
  scale_color_gradient2(
    low = "#b5414d",
    mid = "#d8d1c2",
    high = "#286f9e",
    midpoint = 0
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Democratic minus Republican two-party margin (percentage points)",
    y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    axis.text = element_text(color = "#29445f"),
    axis.title.x = element_text(color = "#66717a", size = 10),
    plot.margin = margin(12, 14, 8, 8)
  )

plotly::ggplotly(margin_chart, tooltip = c("x", "y"), height = 390) |>
  plotly::config(displayModeBar = FALSE, responsive = TRUE)
```

<p class="map-source"><strong>Sources:</strong> California Secretary of State, <a href="https://www.sos.ca.gov/elections/prior-elections/statewide-election-results/general-election-nov-5-2024/statement-vote">November 5, 2024 Statement of Vote</a>, President by County (XLSX); county boundaries: U.S. Census Bureau, <a href="https://www.census.gov/geographies/mapping-files/time-series/geo/tiger-line-file.2024.html">2024 TIGER/Line County shapefile</a>.</p>
:::

::: {.map-status}
<p class="map-kicker">A NOTE ON ELECTION SHIFTS</p>

### No 2024–2026 shift map

The county-level 2026 results shown here are for a gubernatorial primary; the historical map is for the 2024 presidential general election. Those are different offices and election types, so comparing their county margins would not measure a meaningful election shift.
:::

:::
